findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:603 — `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `PRCommentWorkflow` composes the integration (e.g., `OpenPRCommentWorkflow.__init__(self, integration: CommitContextIntegration)`) rather than inheriting from it, so every merged-PR comment will raise `AttributeError` at runtime unless the inheritance is verified or the helpers are moved onto `PRCommentWorkflow`

[Medium/data] src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~130 — `zip(error_ids, events.values())` misaligns IDs with data because Nodestore's `get_multi` omits missing nodes instead of returning `None` placeholders, so if any error event is missing (e.g., purged by retention), every subsequent `ErrorEvent` gets the wrong `id`, `title`, and `message`; results should be looked up by `node_id` instead of zipping positional values

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:~43 — `url = serializers.URLField()` restricts URLs to Django's `URLValidator` default schemes (http/https/ftp/ftps), so valid browser report URLs with other schemes (e.g., `android-app://`, `chrome-error://`, `about:`) now fail validation and reject the entire batch with 422, whereas the previous code accepted any string; use `CharField` or a validator with an expanded scheme set

[Medium/performance] src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~118 — `fetch_error_details` performs an unbounded nodestore `get_multi` (one fetch per error ID, and a replay can reference hundreds of errors) synchronously in the request path with no cap on `error_ids`, adding significant latency to the summarize endpoint; consider batching/limiting

[Low/bug] src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:~50 — the age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness (`self.initial_data.get("age")`) instead of key presence, so `age: 0` alongside `timestamp` (or `timestamp: 0` alongside `age`) bypasses the exclusivity validation; additionally, reports containing neither field pass validation despite the docstrings implying one must be present

[Low/bug] src/sentry/preprod/api/endpoints/organization_preprod_artifact_assemble.py:81 — `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` fires before the `features.has("organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble", ...)` check, so requests that are immediately rejected (feature disabled) are counted as assemble events, skewing the metric; move the record call after the feature/permission gate unless counting rejected demand is intentional

[Low/bug] src/sentry/grouping/parameterization.py:~348 — removing the `isinstance(..., ParameterizationCallableExperiment)` branch means any remaining `ParameterizationRegex` experiment in a grouping config would be invoked as `experiment.run(content, _incr_counter)`, passing a 2-arg callable into `pattern.sub`, which calls it with a single match argument, causing a `TypeError`; `_handle_regex_match` is also now dead code, and `ParameterizationRegex` should be removed from the experiment set entirely

[Low/performance] src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~68 — the Snuba `query_replay_instance` call runs unconditionally, even when `enable_error_context=false` and the results will be discarded; skip the query when error fetching is disabled

[Low/api] src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~67 — the endpoint now derives `start`/`end` from `get_filter_params`, which defaults to the last 24 hours when the client sends no period params, so replays older than that window return no rows, `error_ids` is silently empty, and error context quietly disappears for older replays unless the caller always sends an explicit time range

[Low/data] src/sentry/migrations/0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py:8 (and 0920) — gutting already-merged migrations to no-ops is only safe if they truly never ran in any environment; since 0917's original body lacked the `owner_id__isnull=False` filter, any environment where it did run would have `GroupSearchView` rows with NULL `user_id` that the rerevised 0921 migration must account for/clean up

goldens.comment: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:603 — `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but `PRCommentWorkflow` composes the integration (e.g., `OpenPRCommentWorkflow.__init__(self, integration: CommitContextIntegration)`) rather than inheriting from it, so every merged-PR comment will raise `AttributeError` at runtime unless the inheritance is verified or the helpers are moved onto `PRCommentWorkflow`

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py`, the newly added `CommitContextIntegration.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template(...)` calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title(title)`, but the truncation helper added in this diff is `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(...)` (a `@staticmethod` on the integration class). Nothing in the diff adds `_truncate_title` to `PRCommentWorkflow`, so this reference is inconsistent and will raise at runtime when generating merged-PR issue lines (either `AttributeError` if `PRCommentWorkflow` exists without that method, or even `NameError` if it isn’t in scope). The call should use `self._truncate_title(...)` / `CommitContextIntegration._truncate_title(...)` or move the helper onto `PRCommentWorkflow`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:~43 — `url = serializers.URLField()` restricts URLs to Django's `URLValidator` default schemes (http/https/ftp/ftps), so valid browser report URLs with other schemes (e.g., `android-app://`, `chrome-error://`, `about:`) now fail validation and reject the entire batch with 422, whereas the previous code accepted any string; use `CharField` or a validator with an expanded scheme set

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `BrowserReportSerializer` changed `url` from an unvalidated dataclass `str` to `serializers.URLField()`. DRF/Django `URLField` uses Django’s `URLValidator` default `schemes` (http/https/ftp/ftps) unless overridden, so reports whose `url` uses other real-world browser schemes (e.g. `chrome-error://`, `about:`, `android-app://`) would now fail `.is_valid()` and the endpoint returns 422 for the entire batch. The previous implementation would have accepted any string for `url`, so this is a behavior-breaking validation regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~118 — `fetch_error_details` performs an unbounded nodestore `get_multi` (one fetch per error ID, and a replay can reference hundreds of errors) synchronously in the request path with no cap on `error_ids`, adding significant latency to the summarize endpoint; consider batching/limiting

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `fetch_error_details(project_id, error_ids)` in `project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py`, which builds `node_ids = [Event.generate_node_id(...) for id in error_ids]` and then calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` synchronously on the request path. `error_ids` comes directly from `query_replay_instance(...)->process_raw_response(...)->response[0].get('error_ids', [])` with no limiting/capping or batching. This is a concrete performance/scalability concern added by the change (even though it’s a single `get_multi` call, it can still be unbounded in size).

It implicitly recommends checking key presence rather than truthiness, aligning with the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] src/sentry/grouping/parameterization.py:~348 — removing the `isinstance(..., ParameterizationCallableExperiment)` branch means any remaining `ParameterizationRegex` experiment in a grouping config would be invoked as `experiment.run(content, _incr_counter)`, passing a 2-arg callable into `pattern.sub`, which calls it with a single match argument, causing a `TypeError`; `_handle_regex_match` is also now dead code, and `ParameterizationRegex` should be removed from the experiment set entirely

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the `isinstance(..., ParameterizationCallableExperiment)` branch and stops using `_handle_regex_match`, making `_handle_regex_match` effectively dead code (it’s still defined but no longer referenced). It also narrows `ParameterizationExperiment` to only `ParameterizationCallableExperiment`, implying regex-based experiments are no longer supported. However, the finding’s core claim of a *definite* runtime `TypeError` depends on there being “remaining `ParameterizationRegex` experiment(s) in a grouping config,” which is not shown in the diff; it’s a plausible risk (since Python doesn’t enforce the new type alias at runtime), but not verifiable here. What is verifiable is the incomplete cleanup/inconsistency: regex path removed while regex-related code remains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~68 — the Snuba `query_replay_instance` call runs unconditionally, even when `enable_error_context=false` and the results will be discarded; skip the query when error fetching is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the code calls `query_replay_instance(...)` and processes its response to compute `error_ids` *before* checking `enable_error_context` (see the new `disable_error_fetching` block). When `enable_error_context=false`, `error_events` is set to `[]` and the Snuba-derived `error_ids` are not used, so the Snuba query is unnecessary overhead in that case. This is a performance/efficiency issue, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:~67 — the endpoint now derives `start`/`end` from `get_filter_params`, which defaults to the last 24 hours when the client sends no period params, so replays older than that window return no rows, `error_ids` is silently empty, and error context quietly disappears for older replays unless the caller always sends an explicit time range

adjudication.rationale: In `ProjectReplaySummarizeBreadcrumbsEndpoint.get`, the new error-context flow queries Snuba via `query_replay_instance(...)` using `start`/`end` from `self.get_filter_params(request, project)` and then derives `error_ids` as `response[0].get("error_ids", []) if response else []`. There is no fallback if the replay is outside that time window; it will simply produce an empty `error_ids` list and therefore skip adding error context, with no indication besides silently returning fewer logs. This behavior is introduced by the diff (previously no time-windowed replay-instance lookup existed).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] src/sentry/migrations/0917_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.py:8 (and 0920) — gutting already-merged migrations to no-ops is only safe if they truly never ran in any environment; since 0917's original body lacked the `owner_id__isnull=False` filter, any environment where it did run would have `GroupSearchView` rows with NULL `user_id` that the rerevised 0921 migration must account for/clean up

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows migrations 0917 and 0920 were changed from performing SavedSearch→GroupSearchView conversions to unconditional no-ops (both now just `return` with comments pointing to a separate 0921 migration). The finding’s concern is about the safety of modifying already-merged migrations and the potential historical impact of 0917’s prior lack of an `owner_id__isnull=False` filter (0917 originally would have used `user_id=saved_search.owner_id`, which could be NULL, whereas 0920 previously added that filter). The diff itself does not show whether 0921 exists or whether it cleans up any previously-created NULL `user_id` rows, so it’s not a directly verifiable defect from this PR alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded migration-safety/data-integrity concern created by making these migrations no-ops.
